structure: Part 1 read the whole of PROGRAMME-NOTES.md (lines 1-247), the DR1 parity union programme notes, every word. It is a Markdown build-run notes file: a title and preamble (1-5), then twelve level-2 sections in order: What the backlog is (7-14); Standing rulings - do not re-raise these (16-29, one table Increment | Ruling with 5 rows: inc-062, inc-094, inc-030, inc-031, inc-013); The dashboard and the address book are blocked as groups (31-55, Rhys 2026-08-28, 17 dashboard + 2 address-book-scoping increments, the six pickers note); The address space is blocked while the team works in it (57-90, Rhys 2026-09-04, 6 + 4 + 2 blocked, 5 left todo, EUDPA-399 parked); Reference-data lists come from MDM, not from this backlog (92-139, Rhys 2026-09-07, inc-081, inc-071, inc-127 blocked, inc-106/107/110 excluded); inc-161 carries its own design decision (141-161, rule (b), seven templates, inc-006 ordering, 29 not 41 screens); Seven increments disagree about banding (163-176, inc-091); Provenance, and why ids look odd (178-190); Evidence lives in the per-run reports (192-207, one code block of report paths); Pins (209-217, one code block); Target (219-226); Disputed increments are deferred to their own pass (228-247, inc-103, inc-126, inc-145). Claims follow the file's order, one per ruling, blocked group, live defect, exception, ordering constraint and process rule; inc ids are union-backlog ids as the notes use them. Three gaps record where the notes leave a decision open.
